doc.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Marriage, family and the Capitol albums
title: Favorite arrangers, Lush Life and Shearing
summary: She names Gerald Wilson and Jimmy Jones, praises Lush Life, and recalls George Shearing playing on her album's 40th year at Carnegie Hall.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Gerald Wilson and Jimmy Jones. I got a letter from Billy May once. It said that he was glad that God allowed him to live at a time when we could record. I’m trying to remember the song that it was about. But that was nice to hear.
He did your Lush Life album.
That was what he was talking about. That was the one. That’s still my favorite album.
Even Shearing came on board for an orchestration.
Hello Young Lovers, George Shearing. Beautiful charts. I’m trying to remember who worked with him, who wrote the charts out. I can see him, but I can’t call his name.

But I loved George Shearing. He was precious. We did – when we worked at Carnegie Hall – I think it was – I don’t know who we were celebrating. Celebrating somebody’s birthday. I don’t think it was mine. Anyway, Shearing played the music that many years later exactly the way it was played on the record.
Yes, Shearing’s 80th birthday. That he would come in and play the things that we did 40 years ago.
